comparison: Perfect agreement on in vitro experimental findings (C78-C81). Both recognize the demonstration of oxalate metabolism without O. formigenes as supporting metabolic redundancy. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical analysis (ANOVA p<0.001) while peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of the 'independent in vivo and in vitro models' strength.

Perfect agreement on study limitations (C107, C122). Both accept the authors' acknowledgment that formate measurements are confounded and the cooperation hypothesis remains inconclusive. OpenEval explicitly praises this 'honest assessment of uncertainty' while peer reviewers implicitly accept it without challenge.

Perfect agreement on acknowledged limitations (C120, C121). Both accept that host genetics and batch effects represent additional complexity. OpenEval notes these are 'appropriately acknowledged' while peer reviewers do not challenge these stated limitations.

Both evaluate the proposed workflow (C115-C119, C126-C127) as UNCERTAIN, though with different emphases. OpenEval questions generalizability beyond the single case study, calling it 'speculative.' Peer reviewers note 'partial support' and acknowledge Phase III innovation requires further development, stating it's 'challenging' to present unfamiliar complex systems concepts conclusively.

Strong agreement on fecal transplant and transcriptomic findings (C46-C52). OpenEval emphasizes the well-controlled experimental design and appropriate statistical analysis (FDR<0.05). Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the 'multidisciplinary approach' including 'fecal transplant' and 'hepatic response-transcriptomics,' with editor confirming data are 'solid.'

Strong agreement on metabolomics findings (C53-C59). OpenEval supports the untargeted metabolomics with appropriate statistics and integration with transcriptomics. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'untargeted metabolomics' as part of the multidisciplinary approach and confirm data are 'solid,' though they group these claims with transcriptomics rather than evaluating separately.

Strong agreement on metagenomic findings (C60-C69). OpenEval supports the shotgun metagenomic data and longitudinal design, noting redundancy inference would benefit from functional validation. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize 'longitudinal analysis' and 'deep bioinformatic analyses of the genomes assembled' as strengths, confirming data are 'solid.'

Strong agreement on genome analysis findings (C70-C77). OpenEval supports the comprehensive analysis of 248 high-quality genomes, noting HGT inference relies on citation rather than direct evidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge the 'deep bioinformatic analyses of the genomes assembled' as part of the metagenomic work, confirming data are 'solid.'

Strong agreement on in vivo transplant experiments (C82-C87). OpenEval calls this 'strongly supported' with appropriate controls and statistics, identifying the non-additive effect of O. formigenes as a 'central finding.' Peer reviewers explicitly recognize 'development of synthetic microbial communities' and their 'evaluation in vivo' as key strengths, calling it a 'valuable finding.'

Strong agreement on 16S rRNA sequencing findings (C88-C92). OpenEval supports the findings on within-group variation and recovery, noting functional redundancy over taxonomic composition. Peer reviewers group these with the broader in vivo experiments, acknowledging the overall approach as demonstrating metabolic redundancy.

Agreement on differential effectiveness between cohorts (C93-C95). OpenEval supports the comparison but notes batch effects complicate direct comparison. Peer reviewers accept the overall in vivo findings as 'valuable,' implicitly accepting these cohort comparisons as part of the broader experimental validation.

Agreement on primary conclusions about redundancy (C96-C101). OpenEval emphasizes the 'stepwise experimental approach' providing 'strong converging support' for redundancy as the primary mechanism. Peer reviewers acknowledge the 'multidisciplinary approach' and confirm findings are 'solid,' though they evaluate the overall conclusion more broadly in R4.

Partial overlap on conclusions and theoretical framework (C96). OpenEval strongly supports the primary conclusion with converging evidence. Peer reviewers rate the broader theoretical framework as UNCERTAIN, noting 'partial support' for the complex systems approach despite accepting the experimental findings.

Strong agreement on main findings summary (C102-C106). OpenEval emphasizes 'compelling' evidence for redundancy over cooperation with 'robust support from multiple experimental systems.' Peer reviewers explicitly call this a 'valuable finding on the oxalate-microbiome-host system,' confirming metabolic redundancy as the key conclusion.

Divergent evaluations of ecological/evolutionary context (C108-C111). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, calling inferences 'reasonable' with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting 'partial support' for the complex systems theoretical approach, suggesting these broader contextual claims need further development.

Agreement on some contextual claims (C108, C110). OpenEval supports these as reasonable inferences from data and literature. Peer reviewers do not challenge these specific methodological foundations, implicitly accepting them as part of the experimental design.

Strong agreement on main conclusions (C123-C125). OpenEval states these are 'well-supported by integrated experimental evidence' and 'directly address the study objectives.' Peer reviewers call this a 'valuable finding,' confirming metabolic redundancy as the key mechanistic insight.

Agreement on N. albigula natural history connection (C125). OpenEval supports this conclusion as connecting findings to natural history with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the methodological foundations without challenge.

Agreement on literature-based background (C1-C13). OpenEval confirms all claims are 'supported by appropriate citations' establishing rationale and knowledge gaps. Peer reviewers do not challenge these background claims, with editor's acceptance implicitly supporting these foundational statements.

Agreement on theoretical framework background (C14-C23). OpenEval confirms these complex systems claims are 'appropriately cited' and establish conceptual foundation. Peer reviewers do not challenge the background literature, though they later express uncertainty about the application of this framework (see R5, R7).

Agreement on oxalate biology background (C24-C42). OpenEval confirms 'comprehensive background' with 'appropriate citations' providing 'strong rationale.' Peer reviewers acknowledge the study uses 'the well-studied oxalate-microbiome-host system' and recognize variable clinical trial outcomes as motivation, implicitly accepting this background.

Agreement on clinical motivation (C43-C45). OpenEval confirms these claims are 'supported by citations to published meta-analyses' establishing clinical motivation. Peer reviewers acknowledge variable clinical trial outcomes as study motivation, implicitly accepting these foundational claims.

Agreement on methodological details (C128-C133). OpenEval confirms methods are 'supported by citations' and models are 'appropriate and well-characterized.' Peer reviewers do not question these methodological foundations, with editor's statement that data are 'solid' implicitly accepting experimental design elements.

Agreement on genome quality metrics (C134-C135). OpenEval notes quality metrics 'meet current standards' (248 genomes, >80% complete, >90% pure). Peer reviewers explicitly recognize 'deep bioinformatic analyses of the genomes assembled' as a strength, implicitly accepting these quality standards.

Agreement on abstract's main findings (C3-C5). OpenEval confirms these 'accurately summarize the study's key contributions' and are 'well-supported by detailed experimental results.' Peer reviewers acknowledge the 'multidisciplinary approach' and confirm findings are 'solid,' accepting these summary statements.
